thread:
ana: heads-up — we saw a p95/p99 token-latency spike on canary (model v2.3.1) right after a 15s traffic burst. correlate shows KV eviction bursts at the same time. :eyes:
perfbot: alert: canary:v2.3.1 p99_token_latency > 450ms (window 5m) — env=prod-canary — trace_id=0x8f3a
liam: can you paste the flame/profile? curious if kernel selection or batching widened the critical path
ana: (typo) ana: linking the flame + kv timeline: https://dash.redwood.internal/flame/0x8f3a and a small CSV of eviction_count by host
pat: quick read: eviction spikes line up with batcher backpressure events. looks like large batches + sudden eviction = extra memcpy + cache misses.
sophia: interesting — kernel selection might be choosing the large-seq attention kernel for many requests because our sequence heuristic uses max_seq in batch. that + eviction thrashing could blow up token latency
liam: makes sense. two orthogonal fixes to try: (1) make kernel selector use median/95th instead of max for mixed seq batches (2) conservative eviction smoothing during canaries
pat: agree. also suspect reactor scheduling when big batches queue — maybe we should cap batch size by kv_cache_hit_rate per worker
mike: i can add a temporary per-route KPI on the model-compare dashboard: p50/p95/p99 token-latency, token_cost, kv_hit_rate, batch_size_distribution. we need tags: model_version, rollout_id, route
ana: (again typo) ana: here's a quick debug flag to repro locally + on canary: ```yaml
runtime:
  debug:
    kv_instrumentation: true
    kernel_selector_override: auto->median_based
    batcher_window_ms: 12
    eviction_smoothing_ms: 200
```
liam: nice. run with eviction_smoothing_ms=200 first, collect 30m of traces, then flip kernel_selector_override. keep the same traffic shape so we isolate variables
sophia: for dashboards: token-level latency breakdown needed (gen overhead, kernel_exec, memcpy, kv_lookup, scheduling). current token breakdown only shows gen vs inference. add new panels and a stacked bar for token components
pat: also add a small heatmap: batch_size vs sequence_length vs p99_token_latency. that shows mixed-short+long batches causing bad kernel picks
mike: will add panels and an explainer note per-panel. I'll tag them with rollout_id so we can compare canary vs control in the same time window
ana: (typo) ana: commit to runtime toggles: 9b3d5c4 — includes kernel selector switch and eviction smoothing. pushed to canary at 1765431980
perfbot: deploy: canary runtime 9b3d5c4 -> success (zones: us-west-2a/us-west-2b)
liam: post-deploy profile (first 10m) shows median token latency unchanged, but p99 reduced ~30ms when eviction_smoothing=200. good sign
sophia: but we still see occasional >400ms outliers tied to batcher spikes. next step: try kernel_selector_override=median_based on a 10% traffic slice
pat: +1. also adjust batcher_window_ms from 12->8 to reduce latency for short sequences, see effect on throughput
mike: scheduling: I'll create a model-compare tab that overlays v2.3.0 (control) vs v2.3.1 (canary) with per-route filters and the new token-component charts. ETA 2h.
nana: (typo) ana: after that we can run a short A/B with 5% traffic for 1h, check p99 token latency, kv_hit_rate, and token_cost. if stable, ramp
liam: if p99 still breaches, rollback canary and we iterate on kernel heuristics or add an ad-hoc batching isolation for long sequences
sophia: FYI add tags in traces: model_version, rollout_id, kernel_choice, batch_size, kv_eviction_count so dashboards can slice/aggregate properly
pat: I'll add a small experiment to disable eviction temporarily on one node pool to validate causality
mike: created dashboard: https://dash.redwood.internal/d/compare/kv-evict-compare (will be live in ~10m). panels include token-component breakdown, heatmap, p99 trend by route and model_version
ana: thanks all. summary: (1) eviction_smoothing=200 helped p99 a bit (2) plan A/B kernel selector change on 10% (3) dashboards + tags added for quick triage (4) experiment disabling eviction on small pool
liam: perfect. I'll watch the dashboard and ping if regressions pop up. :thumbsup:
perfbot: note: create incident if p99_token_latency > 500ms for 10m across any route — automated pager will fire.
